title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's notes on the standard conjectures, where abelian varieties serve as the test case. Here he works out how a homomorphism of abelian varieties acts on ℓ-adic cohomology. Throughout, H^*(A) = Λ^* H^1(A), and H^1(A) is dual to the rational Tate module T_{Q_ℓ}(A).

(3) Equal dimensions. Let u: A'→A be a homomorphism with dim A = dim A' = n. He first wrote 'isogénie', then crossed it out and replaced it with 'morphisme'. The pullback on top cohomology, u^{2n}: H^{2n}(A) ≅ Q_ℓ(-n) → H^{2n}(A') ≅ Q_ℓ(-n), is multiplication by deg u = d. This is zero exactly when u is not surjective, i.e. when u is not an isogeny. Dualising by Poincaré duality ('par transposition') gives a Gysin-type map u_* with u_*(1) = d·1.

General dimensions n, n'. Transposing the pullback via the Poincaré duality isomorphisms η_A, η_{A'} gives a Gysin map H^i → H^{i+2(n'-n)}(n'-n). This map is determined purely by linear algebra from u^1 on H^1, because u^* = Λ^*(u^1).

Next page. For u: A→A' (dim m → n'), u_*(1_A) ∈ H^{2(n'-m)}(A')(n'-m) is the class of the image cycle. Precisely, it equals d·γ(B), where B = u(A) and d is the degree of A→B, and it is 0 if dim u(A) < m. Linear-algebraically, take u_1: T(A) → T(A') on Tate modules:
- if u_1 is not injective, the answer is 0;
- if it is injective, one gets a multivector of degree 2(n'-m) = dim coker u_1, i.e. an alternating form on T(A') attached to the cokernel.

Purpose: show that, for abelian varieties, cycle classes of images of homomorphisms and Gysin maps are explicitly computable from Tate-module data. This is input for checking the Lefschetz/Hodge-type standard conjectures on abelian varieties.
errors: Direction/notation slip. For u: A'→A, the transpose of u^*: H^*(A)→H^*(A') is a map H^*(A')→H^*(A), so one expects u_*(1_{A'}) = d·1_A. The page instead writes u_*: H^*(A)→H^*(A') and u_*(1_A) = d·1_{A'}.

In the general-dimension paragraph, 'u^1: H^1(A')→H^1(A)' also runs in the direction appropriate to u: A→A', which is the convention adopted on the next page. The roles of A and A' are swapped mid-argument. This is harmless but inconsistent.
Convention: deg u is implicitly set to 0 when u is not surjective. This is fine but should be stated.

ideas.what: Pullback on top-degree cohomology of an abelian variety is multiplication by the degree; dually u_*(1) = deg(u)·1.
ideas.modern_name: Degree of a finite morphism / projection formula, Gysin map
ideas.where_published: Standard; cf. SGA 4½ cycle class, SGA 5

ideas.what: Gysin map defined as the Poincaré-dual transpose of the pullback, H^i(A)→H^{i+2(n'-n)}(A')(n'-n), computed from Λ^* of u^1 on H^1.
ideas.modern_name: Gysin / proper pushforward on cohomology of abelian varieties
ideas.where_published: Not in a specific Grothendieck text to my knowledge

ideas.what: The class of an abelian subvariety (image of a homomorphism) is determined linear-algebraically by the Tate-module map: the degree times a decomposable multivector of degree 2·codim attached to the cokernel.
ideas.modern_name: Cohomology class of abelian subvarieties via Tate modules / Plücker-type description
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; used by Lieberman (1968) and Kleiman in proofs of the standard conjectures for abelian varieties
ideas.where_published: Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (in Dix exposés, 1968); Lieberman 1968

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine computations about Gysin maps and classes of abelian subvarieties, preparing the treatment of the standard conjectures for abelian varieties. That material was published by Lieberman and Kleiman around 1968. Nothing here is new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Line 'Supposons que…': the image reads 'u^1 : H^1(A') → H^1(A)  (d'où u^* : H^*(A') → H^*(A) par Λ^*)'. The first map is u^1 on H^1, not u^* on H^*.
Header correction: 'isogénie' is struck out and replaced by 'morphisme, avec dim A = dim A' = n' (interlinear addition).
The isomorphisms under H^{2n} read Q_ℓ(-n) for both A and A'.
